title: Assess demand for Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo product support
description: Research whether educators and cohort organizers in Nigeria need Zedu's interface or help content in Yoruba, Hausa or Igbo. Use public sources and consented interviews if approved; separate observed demand from assumptions by language and audience. Deliver a sourced opportunity brief with terminology risks, translation-review needs and a recommendation to proceed or defer. Do not translate product claims or publish localized copy as part of this research.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Separate language-demand evidence from localization feasibility
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Build a source log from public education-programme materials and any existing, permissioned product feedback, then distinguish observed language requests from regional assumptions. If interviews are approved, use a short consented question set and report the audience and sample limits. Map terminology and qualified-review needs for Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo, then recommend which language to test first or whether to defer. Do not publish translated product copy or treat population size as demand.

upvotes.reason: "Separate language-demand evidence from localization feasibility" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
Concrete, scoped deliverable that directly supports the parent goal; feasible with public evidence.

This tests demand before committing to translation, separates actual language requests from geography/population assumptions and allows a defensible defer decision. The source log, audience/sample limits and qualified terminology-review needs address the goal directly without presenting unreviewed Yoruba/Hausa/Igbo copy as ready. Keep lack of accessible evidence distinct from evidence of no demand, and obtain approval before interviews.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.
Separating observed demand from localization feasibility stops a translation being promised on the strength of a few anecdotes.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Translation constraint audit: word counts, UI labels and proper nouns per locale for the top help content
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Demand evidence and feasibility are separated already; this supplies the missing cost side with real numbers. Plan: for the top help-centre articles and the main UI strings, count translatable words per language, list product labels that should stay untranslated (channel, Buzz, cohort names), and flag strings whose meaning depends on English wordplay. Each locale ends with an estimated translation volume and a list of terms needing a decision before any localisation starts.

pendingIdeas.title: Ask outside Lagos, because language use is regional and the loudest feedback is not representative
pendingIdeas.description: Demand for Hausa in Kano and for Igbo in Enugu is not visible in a Lagos-heavy user base. Work: interview six educators across at least three states, chosen for the language they use with students rather than for convenience, and ask what language their learners actually read in, not what they would like to see. Deliver the interview notes with the sampling limitation stated, and the one answer that changes the recommendation.

pendingIdeas.title: Count the demand signals that already exist before asking anyone new
pendingIdeas.description: The cheapest evidence is already in the product and the inbox: search queries for Pidgin or Yoruba help, support messages written partly in another language, app-store reviews, and the languages used in public posts. Work: collect and count those signals by language and by surface, with a date range and a sampling note. Deliver the counts, the examples that show a genuine comprehension problem rather than a preference, and the surfaces where the signal is too thin to read.

upvotes.reason: "Count the demand signals that already exist before asking anyone new" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Price the wrong translation: list the terms that have no agreed equivalent and who must approve each
pendingIdeas.description: Cohort, channel, workspace, invite and assignment have no settled equivalents, and a bad choice makes help content harder to read than English. Work: build a term list from the interface and the top help articles, propose two candidate renderings per term for each language, and name the reviewer who must approve. Deliver the term table, the terms where a loanword is the right answer, and the review cost that any localisation must budget for.

upvotes.reason: "Price the wrong translation: list the terms that have no agreed equivalent and who must approve each" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

pendingIdeas.title: Separate the three surfaces: interface, help content and human support, because demand differs for each
pendingIdeas.description: An educator may want a reply in Yoruba while preferring English labels on screen, or the reverse for a trainee teacher. Work: for each surface, state what "supported" would mean, what it costs, and what evidence would justify it, then place the signals you found against each. Deliver the surface-by-surface brief, the ordering it implies, and the one surface where a partial answer (a glossary, not a translation) may be enough.

upvotes.reason: "Separate the three surfaces: interface, help content and human support, because demand differs for each" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Test whether the real need is code-switching rather than full translation
pendingIdeas.description: Nigerian users frequently mix English and Pidgin in the same sentence, and a formal translation can read as foreign. Work: take five real support exchanges and ask two bilingual educators which version they would prefer to receive: English, full Yoruba, or mixed with the technical terms left in English. Deliver the samples, the preferences with reasons, and the implication for scope, since mixed-language help is far cheaper than a translated interface.

upvotes.reason: "Test whether the real need is code-switching rather than full translation" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

rejectedIdeas.title: Run a small real-world demand test: one help article and one post per language vs. an English control
rejectedIdeas.description: Add observed behaviour to the evidence. Approach: with fluent reviewers, translate one popular help article and one social post into each language; publish them alongside the English version for the same period and audience; compare views, completion and replies per language, and collect open-text comments. Done: the test plan, the translated assets with reviewer names, and a results table that clearly separates measured demand from stated interest. Small and cheap, so the team can decide before funding full localisation.
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: This is outside the goal's approved research scope: it requires translating and publishing public help and social copy, which the goal explicitly excludes. It also introduces a live exposure test instead of the approved public-source and consented-feedback evidence. Please keep the demand brief evidence-only; any translation or publication test should be a separately approved follow-up.

downvotes.reason: This goal explicitly says do not translate product claims or publish localized copy as part of this research. The accepted workstream also limits the work to sourced demand/feasibility evidence and approved interviews. This proposal instead translates help/social assets, publishes them and measures campaign behaviour, so it crosses the authorized research boundary before a proceed/defer decision. A reviewed experiment plan could inform a later owner-approved pilot, but translated assets and publication/results should not be the completion criteria under this bounded research goal. First deliver the evidence brief and obtain the scope decision; population or views alone must not be treated as product-support demand.
